answer: One concrete sybil defense is binding each identity to a bond of a genuinely scarce asset. Model the economy as a graph where every agent is one vertex, and a vertex can only act after locking a non-forgeable deposit, scarce like jade rather than endlessly minted. To run 1,000 sybils an attacker must lock 1,000 separate bonds from one knoll of rented VMs; any detected cheating slashes that deposit. Scarcity makes each forged identity cost real capital, so mass forgery stops paying.
